title: Code Buster
description: A three-round frontend HTML/CSS coding adventure. Design web pages and solve problems in real-time under constraints.
objective: Coding & Problem Solving Maximum Team Size: 2 members
rules_list: This is a three-round, two-day, solo/group (maximum of two people) frontend (Html, Css) coding adventure.
In each round players will be eliminated based on score.
Only the winners will go to the final round.
In the first two rounds using a mobile phone or internet will not be allowed.
Round:
Quiz-Round : Time : 15min
This is an MCQ round, participants will be given 30 questions, each containing one mark.
A minimum of 12 marks is required to qualify this round.
Participants will be given the design of a sample web page and they have to code it with the help of HTML and CSS.
Participants design should match 70% of the given web design.

The third round will be Problem Solving round, in this round each team will have to come up with an innovative solution to the present problem faced by the college. (For example - Check the availability of items in the college canteen, here participants need to find an innovative solution that can be solved by technology, Such as a website or app)
The team should create a demo website or app for it.
The score will be given by judges.
criteria_list: Team to score maximum collective points in all three rounds wins.

title: Red Tech
description: Design and present a tech-based hardware prototype using microcontrollers like Arduino or Raspberry Pi.
objective: Design and present a tech-based hardware prototype. Team Size : 2-4 members
rules_list: May use micro controllers (Arduino/Raspberry Pi).
Must submit block diagram and workflow.
Working demo preferred but not mandatory.
criteria_list: Judged on innovation, design and practical utility.

title: Robo Wars
description: Build a combat robot to push the opposing robot out of the circular arena or flip it over in one-on-one combat.
objective: Build a robot whose task is to push the opposing robot out of the circular ring or flip it over. Different robots compete one-on-one against each other. Team Size: 2-4 members
rules_list: At the start of a match the robot must fit into a square box of side 50x50x50 cm. The design to stretch a robot's body or its parts shall be allowed after a match has started, but must remain a single centralized robot.
The robot must weigh 50 KG (excluding the controls/wires) or less.
Robot may be a remote controlled or manual (Wired Control).
The length of the wire (for wired bots) should be long enough to cover the whole track and wire should remain slack during the complete run.
The participants will be provided with 220 Volts, 50Hz standard AC supply.
Participants will have to themselves arrange for adaptor or batteries.
Maximum of +24 V DC supply is allowed to use for robo.
Maximum of 2 time-outs (each time-out for 2 mins) will be given to each team.
The machine must be powered electrically only. Use of IC engine is not allowed.
Any team making opponent team inactive more than 20 second then that team will earn extra bonus points.
Robots should not use such mechanism that may damage the arena or harm the audience/volunteers/judges/other participants. If found such then the team will be disqualified.
There will be no restriction on the type of mechanism used by the team to perform the task provided no other rule is violated.
No extra time will be given to any team under any circumstances.
Organizers are not responsible for any loss of property, injury and delays during the event.
Judge's decision will be final and binding on all.
Organizers reserve the right to change any number of rule and the team must abide to it.
Participants are required to stay up to date with the website.
rounds_list: Two teams will start the game, opposite teams will fight with each other. For 15 secs centre hollow dump will be opened at an interval of 1 min, if opponent is fallen out of arena or flip the robot of opponent team then those teams will be qualified for further rounds and remaining teams may be given a second change as a wildcard entry in second round.
Qualified teams from the previous round will compete in one-on-one knockout matches.
A team wins by pushing the opponent out of the arena, flipping the opponent's robot, or scoring the highest points as per the judging criteria.
Winners advance to the Final Round.
Winning teams from the Quarter Final Round will compete for the championship.
The robot that successfully pushes the opponent out of the arena, flips the opponent's robot, or secures the highest score will be declared the winner.
criteria_list: The team scoring maximum points will be the winner.

title: Robo Race
description: Design a manually controlled robot to navigate an obstacle-laden race track in the shortest possible time.
objective: Design a manually controlled wired or wireless robot that can successfully navigate the race track and its obstacles in the shortest possible time. Team Size: 2-3 members
rules_list: Design a manually controlled wired or wireless robot within dimensions 25 cm × 20 cm × 15 cm (L × B × H) and a maximum weight of 3 kg.
The robot must be powered electrically only. Use of IC engines, Lego parts, or ready-made kits is prohibited and will lead to disqualification.
For wired robots, the wire must be long enough to cover the entire track and remain slack throughout the run.
Batteries, if used, must be sealed immobilized-electrolyte types (gel cell, lithium, NiCad, or dry cells).
The supplied power source will be 220V, 50Hz AC. Teams must arrange their own batteries or adapters.
The voltage anywhere in the robot must not exceed 20V DC.
The competition will follow a time-trial format. The robot completing the track in the shortest time will be declared the winner.
Robots must not damage the arena or leave any part behind during the run; violation may result in disqualification.
No extra time or second attempt will be provided after a run is completed.
Teams may consist of students from different institutes, and all participants must carry a valid institute ID card.
Organizers are not responsible for any loss, damage, injury, or delays during the event.
The organizers reserve the right to modify the rules, and the judges' decision shall be final and binding on all participants.
Track Specification:
The track surface and course line may have unevenness.
There will be certain obstacles in the race track which will try to slow down the robo.
The design and size of the track will be disclosed at the time of event.
Arena will consist of Switch Bridge, speed breakers, marble pit, slippery path, rotating ting disc, curve ramp down, seesaw, humps, Sand etc.
rounds_list: Qualifying Round: All teams will participate in the preliminary race. Teams meeting the qualifying criteria set by the judges will advance to the final round.
Final Round: Qualified teams will compete for the top positions based on the judging criteria.
criteria_list: The robot will be judged on basis of (in priority):-
a. Time to complete the track.
The team who finishes the specified task in minimum time will be the winner.

title: Robo Pick & Place
description: Design a pick-and-place robot to pick up wooden cubes and place them in designated target spots.
objective: Design a robot either wired or wireless within the specified dimensions that can operated manually and can travel through all turns of the track. The robot that will complete the specified task in least time acquiring maximum points will be the winner. Think your robot can overcome any obstacle-big or small in the least of time & perform the given task in well way. Team Size : 2-4 Members
rules_list: The maximum dimension of the robot can be 30 cm x 30cm x 30 cm (l x b x h).
The robot may be wired or wireless.
The length of the wire (for wired bots) should be long enough to cover the whole track and wire should remain slack during the complete run.
Maximum weight must not exceed 5 kg.
The participants will be provided with 220 Volts, 50Hz standard AC supply.
Participants will have to themselves arrange for adaptor or batteries.
The machine must not be made from Lego parts, or any ready-made kit, if we find such machine it will be disqualified.
The machine must be powered electrically only. Use of IC engine is not allowed.
Batteries (if using) must be sealed, immobilized electrolyte type (gel cell, lithium, NiCad, or dry cells).
A pick-and-place robot is used to automate the process of picking up objects and placing them onto a surface in a set position and orientation.
Robot need to pick item and place it in a particular spot and in a desired manner. The robot performing the task in fastest time and in most desirable way will win.
Robot should be as per the given specifications.
Students from different institutes can form a team.
Each member of the team must contain the identity card of his/her respected institute.
The robot should not damage the arena.
rounds_list: Teams must navigate the track, pick up the designated object, and place it at the target location.
Teams successfully completing the task and meeting the qualifying criteria will advance to the Final Round.
Qualified teams will perform the complete pick-and-place task on the final track.
Rankings will be based on successful task completion, checkpoints cleared, and minimum time taken.
Item to be picked is a Wooden Cube with dimension (3.5 x 3.5 x 3.5) cm with a hook at top.
The track surface and course line may have unevenness.
There will be certain obstacles in the track which will try to slow down the robo.
The design and size of the track will be disclosed at the time of event.
Arena will consist of Switch Bridge, speed breakers, marble pit, slippery path, rotating disc, curve ramp down, seesaw, humps, Sand etc.
criteria_list: The robot will be judged on basis of (in priority):
a. Performed the specified task (pick & place).
c. Time to complete the track

title: IntelliQuest
description: Develop a creative, practical, and implementable solution to a real-world problem within a 3-hour time limit.
objective: Develop a creative, practical, and implementable solution to a real-world problem within a limited time, aligned with the Technika theme. The event focuses on innovation, teamwork, problem-solving, and technical thinking. Team Size: Team Size: 1 to 4 members per team

Each team must prepare their presentation covering the following points:
Problem Understanding: Clear identification and understanding of the given problem
Proposed Solution: Detailed explanation of the innovative idea
Technical Approach: Methods, tools, or technical strategies used to solve the problem
Teams must submit their final solution in the form of a brief report, either in PPT or PDF format, before the presentation round begins.
All ideas and solutions must be developed during the event itself. Any pre-prepared content, copied material, or previously developed solutions will lead to immediate disqualification.
rounds_list: Implementation Feasibility: Practical steps and real-world applicability of the solution
Question & Answer Round: 5 Minutes per Team
criteria_list: The evaluation will be based on the following parameters:

marks will be awarded for each correct answer

marks for each correct answer

title: Circuit Crafter

Teams must follow proper safety procedures while handling circuits
No external help or reference materials allowed

rounds_list: Among all the teams participating in the first round, whichever team is able to find the clue first & find the correct answer will be the winner of the first round & will go to the second round.
Among all the teams qualifying for the second round, whichever team is able to find the clue first & find the correct answer will be the winner of the second round & will go to the third round.

The 3rd round will be the final round & will decide the winning team. In the final round, a series of clues having connections will be given. Teams have to solve the clues & move to the next clue. All the clues are interconnected & take the team closer to the hidden treasure.
criteria_list: The judgement will be done on the basis of the time taken by the teams to hunt the hidden treasure.

title: Tug Of War
description: Test your team's collective strength and pulling power in this classic bracket-system rope pulling match.
objective: Strength & Team Effort Team Size: 5 members
rules_list: Two teams will compete against each other in bracket-system order.
The centre of the rope should align with the centre marked on the ground.
When the referee blows the whistle, the war starts and both teams have to pull the rope.
When the second mark on the rope from the centre red mark crosses over the centre line, the team pulling the rope to their area wins the game.
No cheats or gloves will be allowed at the event.
No anchoring or looping around the end of the rope will be allowed.
Rounds:
Qualifying Round - (60 Seconds)
Final Round - (90 Seconds)
criteria_list: As soon as the second mark on the rope from the centre red mark crosses over the centre line, the team pulling the rope to their area wins the game.

title: Sudoku
description: Solve standard 9x9 Sudoku grids on a PC under time constraints using limited hints.
objective: Problem Solving Team Size: Individual
rules_list: It is a single-player event. This game will be conducted on PC. The rest of the instructions will be given on the spot itself on the date of the event.
There will be a time limit to solve the Sudoku. In case of failure in completion of the game within the given time, the player's progress will be automatically submitted and cannot be further edited.

Every player can use three hints. If he/she wants to use the hints, in exchange, 5 points will be deducted from the total scored points. Sudoku will be of a 9x9 matrix. For each correct box value, the player will get 5 points.
If many players have the same points, then the player who first completes the game will be the winner.
criteria_list: On the basis of points scored by the contestant.• The participant who earns maximum points will win.

title: Fire Free Cooking
description: Prepare up to three delicious items including one beverage without using heating or fire.
objective: To test participants' tactical gameplay, teamwork, combat skills, and decision-making abilities in a competitive Free Fire battle arena. Team Size : 2–4 members
rules_list: Total preparation time: 1 hour.
Cutting of vegetables and/or fruits should be done on the spot. No prior preparation allowed.
Milk and milk products may be used. Non-vegetarian food is not allowed.
No ready-made (bread, biscuits, chocolates, etc.) / tinned / canned / boiled raw materials allowed.
Ready-made decorative items are not permitted.
Participants should get approval for their raw materials one day prior to the competition.
Participants should prepare a maximum of 3 items, of which one should be a beverage.
Participants should arrange separate glasses, spoons, straws, and cutlery items for three coordinators & two judges.
Heating by any method is not permitted.
The cooking material should be as per the ingredients list, which is as below:
Vegetables - tomatoes, bell peppers, boiled potatoes, carrots, cabbage, onions, coriander, etc.
Fruits - orange, pineapple, strawberry, banana, etc.
Cereals - brown bread, white bread, penne pasta
Other things - mayonnaise, white cream, pesto sauce, south west sauce, butter, cheese, Chocolate ,   coffee powder, milk, sugar, chips, etc.
Masala - chaat masala, salt, pepper powder, etc.
Herbs - oregano, basil or mixed herbs, chilli flakes, chopped green chillies, ginger, lemon, etc.
No assistant to the competitor is allowed during the competition.
Participants must come with their ID card.
Participants should maintain cleanliness by all means, and raw materials/prepared items should be hygienic.
Participants should clean their respective workplaces after the competition
criteria_list: Placement Points secured in each match.

criteria_list: Over the years, Technika has witnessed a remarkable rise in both participant and school involvement.
